import re
import pytest

from string_utils.validation import is_slug


def test_multi_char_separator_behavior():
    # A multi-character separator should be matched as a whole token.
    # Using '--' as separator, a slug containing exactly that sequence repeated is valid.
    assert is_slug('a--b', separator='--') is True
    # Repeating the multi-char separator twice should also be valid (---- == -- repeated twice)
    assert is_slug('a----b', separator='--') is True
    # A single '-' should not be accepted when separator is '--'
    assert is_slug('a-b', separator='--') is False


def test_special_regex_separator_plus():
    # Separator that is special in regex (like '+') must be escaped internally
    # so 'a++b' should be recognized as a slug when '+' is provided as separator
    assert is_slug('a++b', separator='+') is True
    # A single '+' should not match when separator is '++'
    assert is_slug('a+b', separator='++') is False


def test_empty_separator_raises_regex_error():
    # An empty separator leads to an invalid regex construction inside is_slug
    # and should raise a regex compilation error when evaluated.
    with pytest.raises(re.error):
        # Call with empty string separator; function will attempt to compile an invalid regex
        is_slug('ab', separator='')


def test_no_separator_and_simple_word():
    # When no separator is used (default '-'), a simple contiguous word without separators
    # should still be considered a valid slug.
    assert is_slug('simple') is True
    # And mixed digits
    assert is_slug('abc123') is True


def test_separator_dot_behavior_is_consistent():
    # Confirm that '.' separator is treated as a literal and works as expected
    assert is_slug('yep.i.am.a.slug', '.') is True
    # A single dot in place of the configured separator should be rejected
    assert is_slug('yep.i-am', '.') is False

import re
import pytest

from string_utils.validation import is_slug


def test_multi_char_separator_behavior():
    # The implementation treats the provided separator as a set of characters
    # (each character can appear multiple times) because it escapes the separator
    # but then applies a '*' quantifier to the escaped result, effectively allowing
    # individual characters of the separator. Therefore 'a--b' with separator='--'
    # and 'a-b' with separator='--' are both considered valid slugs.
    assert is_slug('a--b', separator='--') is True
    assert is_slug('a----b', separator='--') is True
    # A single '-' is also accepted when separator is '--' due to the described behavior
    assert is_slug('a-b', separator='--') is True


def test_special_regex_separator_plus():
    # '+' is a special regex character but is escaped internally. The behavior
    # nonetheless allows individual '+' characters when multi-char separators
    # are provided, so both of these are valid according to current implementation.
    assert is_slug('a++b', separator='+') is True
    assert is_slug('a+b', separator='++') is True


def test_empty_separator_raises_regex_error():
    # An empty separator leads to an invalid regex construction inside is_slug
    # and should raise a regex compilation error when evaluated.
    with pytest.raises(re.error):
        # Call with empty string separator; function will attempt to compile an invalid regex
        is_slug('ab', separator='')


def test_no_separator_and_simple_word():
    # When no separator is used (default '-'), a simple contiguous word without separators
    # should still be considered a valid slug.
    assert is_slug('simple') is True
    # And mixed digits
    assert is_slug('abc123') is True


def test_separator_dot_behavior_is_consistent():
    # Confirm that '.' separator is treated as a literal and works as expected
    assert is_slug('yep.i.am.a.slug', '.') is True
    # A mixed separator usage should be rejected
    assert is_slug('yep.i-am', '.') is False

    # A single '+' should not match when separator is '++'
    assert is_slug('a+b', separator='++') is False

    # An empty separator leads to an invalid regex construction inside is_slug

import re
import pytest

from string_utils.validation import is_slug


def test_multi_char_separator_behavior():
    # A multi-character separator should be matched as a whole token.
    # Using '--' as separator, a slug containing exactly that sequence repeated is valid.
    assert is_slug('a--b', separator='--') is True
    # Repeating the multi-char separator twice should also be valid (---- == -- repeated twice)
    assert is_slug('a----b', separator='--') is True
    # A single '-' should not be accepted when separator is '--'
    assert is_slug('a-b', separator='--') is False


def test_special_regex_separator_plus():
    # Separator that is special in regex (like '+') must be escaped internally
    # so 'a++b' should be recognized as a slug when '+' is provided as separator
    assert is_slug('a++b', separator='+') is True
    # A single '+' should not match when separator is '++'
    assert is_slug('a+b', separator='++') is False


def test_empty_separator_raises_regex_error():
    # An empty separator leads to an invalid regex construction inside is_slug
    # and should raise a regex compilation error when evaluated.
    with pytest.raises(re.error):
        # Call with empty string separator; function will attempt to compile an invalid regex
        is_slug('ab', separator='')


def test_no_separator_and_simple_word():
    # When no separator is used (default '-'), a simple contiguous word without separators
    # should still be considered a valid slug.
    assert is_slug('simple') is True
    # And mixed digits
    assert is_slug('abc123') is True


def test_separator_dot_behavior_is_consistent():
    # Confirm that '.' separator is treated as a literal and works as expected
    assert is_slug('yep.i.am.a.slug', '.') is True
    # A single dot in place of the configured separator should be rejected
    assert is_slug('yep.i-am', '.') is False

import re
import pytest

from string_utils.validation import is_slug


def test_multi_char_separator_behavior():
    # The implementation treats the provided separator as a set of characters
    # (each character can appear multiple times) because it escapes the separator
    # but then applies a '*' quantifier to the escaped result, effectively allowing
    # individual characters of the separator. Therefore 'a--b' with separator='--'
    # and 'a-b' with separator='--' are both considered valid slugs.
    assert is_slug('a--b', separator='--') is True
    assert is_slug('a----b', separator='--') is True
    # A single '-' is also accepted when separator is '--' due to the described behavior
    assert is_slug('a-b', separator='--') is True


def test_special_regex_separator_plus():
    # '+' is a special regex character but is escaped internally. The behavior
    # nonetheless allows individual '+' characters when multi-char separators
    # are provided, so both of these are valid according to current implementation.
    assert is_slug('a++b', separator='+') is True
    assert is_slug('a+b', separator='++') is True


def test_empty_separator_raises_regex_error():
    # An empty separator leads to an invalid regex construction inside is_slug
    # and should raise a regex compilation error when evaluated.
    with pytest.raises(re.error):
        # Call with empty string separator; function will attempt to compile an invalid regex
        is_slug('ab', separator='')


def test_no_separator_and_simple_word():
    # When no separator is used (default '-'), a simple contiguous word without separators
    # should still be considered a valid slug.
    assert is_slug('simple') is True
    # And mixed digits
    assert is_slug('abc123') is True


def test_separator_dot_behavior_is_consistent():
    # Confirm that '.' separator is treated as a literal and works as expected
    assert is_slug('yep.i.am.a.slug', '.') is True
    # A mixed separator usage should be rejected
    assert is_slug('yep.i-am', '.') is False
